claims.population: The article says Jos has a population of about 900,000 residents based on the 2006 census.
claims.climate: The article gives an altitude of 1,217 m and a tropical savanna climate (Aw). The monthly precipitation normal is about 0.4, 5.1, 13.4, 93.2, 176.5, 207.1, 248.7, 255.5, 181.9, 58.7, 1.2 and 1.2 mm from January to December.
claims.trade: The article calls Jos the trading hub of Plateau State and names the Jos Main market (terminus) and the Kabong or Rukuba Road satellite market in Jos North.
claims.tin: The article says Jos became an important centre for tin mining after large cassiterite deposits were discovered, and is still often called Tin City.
claims.industry: The article lists food processing, beer brewing and the manufacture of cosmetics, soap, rope, jute bags and furniture as other local enterprises; heavy industry produces cement and asbestos cement, crushed stone, rolled steel and tyre retreads. It names Grand Cereals and Oil Mills among industries in Jos South.
claims.museum: The article says the Jos Museum was founded in 1952 and its Pottery Hall holds pottery from across Nigeria and Nok terracotta heads and artefacts dating from 500 BCE to 200 CE.
claims.nok: The article describes the Nok people as skilled artisans from around the Jos area.
